name: Consecutive primes in arithmetic progression below 10^9
description: construct() -> [p, d, k] describing p, p + d, ..., p + (k-1)d with 2 <= k <= 64, 1 <= d <= 5000 and last term at most 10^9. Every term must be prime (deterministic Miller-Rabin) and no prime may lie strictly between consecutive terms. Maximize k; the optimum below 10^9 is 6. Below 10^9 the longest such progressions have six terms (the first starts at 121174811), so the task recovers a six-term progression.

sources.locator: L. J. Lander and T. R. Parkin, Consecutive primes in arithmetic progression (1967). Crossref records inspected (Lander and Parkin 1967; Dubner, Forbes, Lygeros, Mizony, Nelson and Zimmermann 2002). OEIS A006560 inspected: the smallest six consecutive primes in arithmetic progression start at 121174811 with difference 30 (Lander and Parkin), and seven terms need a difference of at least 210. A local segmented sieve over all 50,847,534 primes below 10^9 confirmed that no seven consecutive primes below 10^9 form an arithmetic progression. Erdős Problem #141 page inspected. Below 10^9 the longest such progressions have six terms (the first starts at 121174811), so the task recovers a six-term progression.
